
```{python}
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4missing/master/data-raw/flights_missing/flights_missing.json"
```

## QUESTION 1

1. __Convert values to missing__ Start with a fresh copy of the flights dataset by reading it in from the link provided above (as opposed to starting with the dataset you ended with in the last assignment). Identify data values that are problematic, non-sense or impossible and change them to be missing. In your report include one record example (one row) from your clean data, in the raw JSON format. Your example should display at least one missing value so that we can verify it was done correctly. (Note: JSON will convert NaN's to null). Describe your process for finding values that needed to be changed, and how you changed them.

I checked the numeric delay columns for values that were impossible or not usable, such as negative values like -999 and values written with a plus sign like 1500+. I converted those values to missing so they would not affect the calculations. The JSON example shows one cleaned row.

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
num_of_cols = [col for col in df.columns if col.startswith("num_of")]
minutes_cols = [col for col in df.columns if col.startswith("minutes_delayed")]
clean_cols = num_of_cols + minutes_cols

df_clean = (
    df
    .with_columns([
        pl.when(
            pl.col(col).cast(pl.Utf8).str.contains(r"\+") |
            (pl.col(col).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False) < 0)
        )
        .then(None)
        .otherwise(pl.col(col).cast(pl.Float64, strict=False))
        .alias(col)
        for col in clean_cols
    ])
)

example_json = (
    df_clean
    .filter(pl.any_horizontal([pl.col(col).is_null() for col in clean_cols]))
    .head(1)
    .write_json()
)

print(example_json)
```

## QUESTION 2

2. __Filling in missing data__ For all the "minutes_delayed" columns, fill in any missing values with the median of that column. For the "num_of" columns, fill in missing values with that column's mean.

_Nothing to write/report for this question_

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
df_filled = (
    df_clean
    .with_columns([
        pl.col(col).fill_null(pl.col(col).median()).alias(col)
        for col in minutes_cols
    ])
    .with_columns([
        pl.col(col).fill_null(pl.col(col).mean()).alias(col)
        for col in num_of_cols
    ])
)

df_filled.select(clean_cols).head()
```

## QUESTION 3
 
3. __Display a histogram for num_of_delays_carrier and for minutes_delayed_nas (2 separate histograms in total). Comment on the shape of each one. Also report the mean of each of these columns now that missing values have been filled in.__

The first histogram is right-skewed. Most airport months have a moderate number of carrier delays, but a smaller number have much higher delay counts. The other histogram is strongly right-skewed. Most values are low, but there are a few very large delay totals. This means NAS delay minutes usually stay lower, but some months have extreme delays.

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
(
    ggplot(df_filled, aes(x="num_of_delays_carrier"))
    + geom_histogram()
    + labs(
        title="Distribution of Carrier Delays",
        x="Number of Carrier Delays",
        y="Count"
    )
)
```


```{python}
(
    ggplot(df_filled, aes(x="minutes_delayed_nas"))
    + geom_histogram()
    + labs(
        title="Distribution of NAS Delay Minutes",
        x="NAS Delay Minutes",
        y="Count"
    )
)
```


```{python}
df_filled.select([
    pl.col("num_of_delays_carrier").mean().alias("mean_num_of_delays_carrier"),
    pl.col("minutes_delayed_nas").mean().alias("mean_minutes_delayed_nas")
])
```
